wpa_summary: Black HillsNational Forest,S. Dak., enlarged by the addi tion of alllands of the Sundance National Forest,Wyo.

lead.basis: The order is an operative act on land whose forest designation persists, not a pure textual amendment, so ruling P2 does not reach it; it ends only when a later order or statute names it or expressly redescribes the forest's whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions, and no such instrument is held.

sources.citation: USDA Forest Service, Lands Staff, Establishment and Modification of National Forest Boundaries and National Grasslands: A Chronological Record, 1891-1996 (Washington, Nov. 1997)
USDA Forest Service, Land Areas of the National Forest System, FY2024 Land Areas Report (as-of date unverified)
National Forest Management Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-588, sec. 9, 90 Stat. 2949, 2957, amending sec. 11(a) of the Forest and Rangeland Renewable Resources Planning Act of 1974 (16 U.S.C. 1609(a))

gaps: The Forest Service chronological record mapping this order to the named forest's later actions (consolidation, renaming, redescription), with the text of each later instrument to test whether it names this order or expressly redescribes the whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions.
For a persistence lead: the current Land Areas Report showing the forest or name on 2026-10-14. 16 U.S.C. 1609(a) is context only.

Where the forest the order constituted was later abolished or merged by name but the order also assigned land to another forest (for example EO 870, Holy Cross and Leadville, Holy Cross abolished by PLO 263; EO 801, Pocatello and Cache, Pocatello merged by EO 2179), ruling P7 does not reach it and the lead stays open.

title: Executive Order 5227—Restoring Certain Reserved Lands Occupied as a Home Site or for Fish Cannery Purposes in Tongass National Forest, Alaska and Opening Such Lands to Entry
wpa_summary: Tongass National Forest,Alaska, diminished,and the ex cluded lands restoredto entry under applicableland laws.

lead.basis: Under the 1897 Act (30 Stat. 36) the order reduced the forest's area by excluding the described land, or opened to entry land already excluded; under ruling P1 that single act was exhausted on the order's effective date, after which the land was governed by the general public-land laws rather than by the order.
